classification.difficultyReason: Match familiar scenarios to supplied curves by checking starting values, increasing or decreasing quantities, and smooth changes in rate; trampoline motion requires recognising rounded turning points rather than sharp peaks.

content.prompt: Select the most appropriate graph for each scenario.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The speed of a car as it goes around a corner.

spec.description: Three horizontally paired speed–time options, preserving arrowed axes, labels and the contrasting straight, smooth and abrupt speed changes.
spec.mathematics: A reaches zero speed through straight segments; B has a smooth dip above zero; C has instantaneous vertical changes between positive constant speeds. No numerical scales are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Options are permanent student givens; the correct option is omitted from the question diagram.

answer.worked: The car slows smoothly before and during the corner, then speeds up smoothly afterwards without stopping. Correct answer: B.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The speed of a runner going up a steep hill from a standing start.

spec.description: Three speed–distance options: positive constant speed, increasing speed that levels off, and increasing speed with an increasingly steep graph.
spec.mathematics: B and C begin at zero speed. B is increasing and concave down; C is increasing and concave up. The horizontal axis is Distance, as printed, and has no numerical scale.
spec.answerVisibility: Options are permanent student givens; the supplied answer is stored separately.

answer.worked: The runner starts at zero speed, gains speed, then approaches a steady speed as they continue uphill. Correct answer: B.

children.label: c
children.prompt: The height of a person jumping on a trampoline.

spec.description: Repeated height–time peaks: A has rounded peaks and positive sharp troughs; B has triangular peaks and positive troughs; C has triangular peaks and zero-height troughs.
spec.mathematics: Each option shows three jumps. A depicts changing vertical speed through each jump and retains a positive minimum height. No numerical scale is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Options are permanent student givens; no correct-option marking appears in the diagram.

answer.worked: The height rises and falls repeatedly. The rounded peaks show the person slowing to a momentary stop at the top of each jump before falling. Correct answer: A.

children.label: d
children.prompt: A bowl of hot soup is cooling. It loses heat quickly at first but as time passes, it loses heat more slowly until it is at room temperature.

spec.description: Four temperature–time options kept together for comparison, with complete vertical Temperature labels, horizontal Time labels and arrowed unscaled axes.
spec.mathematics: A decreases then increases; B decreases fastest initially and flattens towards a positive lower temperature; C decreases increasingly steeply to zero; D decreases slowly initially, faster in the middle, then slowly again.
spec.answerVisibility: All four curves are permanent student givens; the correct letter is stored only in the answer.

answer.worked: The temperature decreases steeply at first, then the graph becomes less steep as the soup approaches room temperature. Correct answer: B.
